question: The dimensional formula of $\dfrac{1}{2}\mu_0 H^2$ ($\mu_0$ is the permeability of free space and $H$ is the magnetic field intensity) is
solution:
$\tfrac12\mu_0H^2$ is the energy stored per unit volume in a magnetic field (since $B = \mu_0 H$, it equals $\dfrac{B^2}{2\mu_0}$).

$$\left[\tfrac12\mu_0H^2\right] = \frac{[\text{Energy}]}{[\text{Volume}]} = \frac{[ML^2T^{-2}]}{[L^3]} = [ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$$

Tip: energy density always has the same dimensions as pressure.
